# crosswork_l2vpn_route_policies (Resource)

This resource can manage an L2VPN route policy (policy definition).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "crosswork_l2vpn_route_policies" "example" {
  name = "cwtest-l2-policy"
  statements = [
    {
      name              = "1"
      match_rd_set      = "cwtest-l2-rds"
      set_ext_community = "cwtest-l2-tags"
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the policy. Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, starting with a letter or a digit.

### Optional

- `instance` (String) Select an instance of the provider configuration by its name. Leave it unset to use the default instance.
- `statements` (Attributes Set) Statements of the policy (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--statements))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The id of the object

<a id="nestedatt--statements"></a>
### Nested Schema for `statements`

Required:

- `name` (String) Statement name
- `set_ext_community` (String) Name of the tag set that the statement sets as the extended community (the color)

Optional:

- `match_etag_set` (String) Name of the Etag set that the statement matches
- `match_evpn_route_type_set` (String) Name of the EVPN route type set that the statement matches
- `match_rd_set` (String) Name of the RD set that the statement matches. A statement takes one condition at most.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import crosswork_l2vpn_route_policies.example "<name>"
```
